question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(1), a firm must provide each associated licensee with reasonable access to which of the following for consultation regarding real estate practice issues?
choice_a: The Real Estate Examining Board's legal counsel
choice_c: An independent contractor attorney retained by the firm
choice_d: The firm's business representative for licensing purposes only
explanation: The statute requires a firm to supervise licensees by "providing a licensee with reasonable access to a supervising broker for the purpose of consultation regarding real estate practice issues."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(2)(a), the written statement of procedures a firm must provide to each associated licensee must address handling of which of the following?
choice_a: Leases, agency agreements, offers to purchase, and other documents and records relating to transactions
choice_b: Marketing budgets and advertising placement decisions
choice_c: Commission splits between the firm and the licensee
explanation: A firm must "provide each licensee associated with the firm with a written statement of the procedures under which the firm and licensees...must operate with respect to handling leases, agency agreements, offers to purchase, and other documents and records relating to transactions."

question: A salesperson joins a firm partway through a biennial licensure period. Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(2)(c), at what points must the firm ensure the salesperson holds a valid license?
choice_a: Only once, at the time of hire
choice_b: Only at the salesperson's next license renewal, whenever that falls
choice_c: Before the salesperson becomes associated with the firm, and again at the beginning of each biennial licensure period
choice_d: Only if a complaint is filed against the salesperson
explanation: The firm must, "[b]efore a licensee becomes associated with the firm and at the beginning of each biennial licensure period, ensure that the licensee holds a valid license."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(3), who is responsible for the custody and safety of documents and records relating to transactions that have been submitted to the firm?
choice_b: The individual licensee who prepared the document
explanation: The statute states: "A firm shall be responsible for the custody and safety of all documents and records relating to transactions submitted to the firm as required under sub. (6)(b)."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(4)(a), when must a supervising broker review the agency agreements, offers to purchase, leases, other transaction documents, and trust account records relating to a transaction?
choice_a: Within 24 hours of the documents being signed
choice_b: Only if requested by a party to the transaction
choice_c: Annually, as part of a firm-wide audit
choice_d: Prior to the closing of the transaction
explanation: The supervising broker "shall review all of the following prior to the closing of a transaction," including executed agency agreements, offers to purchase, leases, other documents, and trust account records relating to the transaction.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(4)(b), the supervising broker's required review of transaction documents is limited to which of the following?
choice_a: Verifying that the sale price reflects fair market value
choice_b: Independently investigating the accuracy of every factual representation made in the transaction
choice_c: Confirming a required disclosure statement was provided, confirming any board-approved form was properly completed, and communicating to the licensee any errors apparent on the face of the document
choice_d: Approving or rejecting the transaction before it can proceed to closing
explanation: The review "shall be limited to confirming that a written disclosure statement...has been provided," confirming any board-approved form was used and completed by filling in the blanks consistent with the form's structure, and "communicating to the licensee any errors...that are apparent on the face of the document and known to the person reviewing the document."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(5)(a), what obligation does a firm that is a licensed broker business entity have regarding the duty to supervise licensees?
choice_a: It may choose to supervise licensees itself without delegating to anyone
choice_b: It shall delegate the duty to supervise licensees to a supervising broker who is a licensed individual broker
choice_c: It may delegate supervision only to the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_d: It has no supervisory obligations because it is a business entity rather than an individual
explanation: "A firm that is a licensed broker business entity shall delegate the performance of the duty to supervise licensees associated with the firm to a supervising broker who is a licensed individual broker." This is mandatory, unlike the option given to firms that are not broker business entities.

question: A firm is not a licensed broker business entity and has made no specific delegation of the supervising broker duty. Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(5)(b), who is deemed to be the supervising broker for that firm?
choice_b: The first salesperson hired by the firm
choice_c: No one; the firm has no supervising broker until it makes a delegation
explanation: A firm that is not a licensed broker business entity "may delegate the duty to supervise licensees...but in the absence of a specific supervising broker delegation, the firm itself is deemed to be the supervising broker for that firm."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(5)(c), what must a valid delegation of the duty to supervise licensees include?
choice_a: It must be written, identify the duty delegated, and be signed by or on behalf of the delegating firm and by the broker to whom the delegation is made
choice_b: It must be pre-approved by the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: It must be renewed every 90 days
choice_d: It may be made orally if later confirmed by email
explanation: "A delegation under par. (a) or (b) shall be written and signed by or on behalf of the delegating firm, identify the duty delegated, and be signed by the broker to whom the delegation is made."

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.132(6)(a), after a licensee is told about an error in a document that was identified during the supervising broker's review under sub. (4)(b), what is the licensee responsible for doing?
choice_a: Correcting the error directly on the executed document without consulting the party
choice_b: Reporting the error to the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: Discussing the error with the party the licensee is working with or representing, who then determines whether to request any changes
explanation: "A licensee associated with a firm shall be responsible for discussing with the party with whom the licensee is working with or representing any error communicated to the licensee as provided in sub. (4)(b), and the party shall determine whether to request any changes to address the error."

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 17.03(3), a broker must be associated with only one firm, except when the broker is doing which of the following?
choice_a: Holding a salesperson license concurrently with a broker license
choice_b: Engaging in independent practice under s. 452.30(6)(a), Stats., or acting as business representative for a licensed business entity under s. 452.12(2)(a), Stats.
choice_c: Working fewer than 20 hours per week in real estate practice
choice_d: Supervising fewer than three other licensees
explanation: "A broker shall be associated with only one firm unless the broker is engaging in independent practice under s. 452.30(6)(a), Stats., or acting as business representative for a licensed business entity under s. 452.12(2)(a), Stats."
